claims.text: Temperature-dependent chemical short-range order governs the onset of premelting and melting in HEA nanoparticles.
Chemical short-range order in 3d HEAs is strongly modulated by Cr atoms having negative atomic stress.
Increasing the effective contribution of Cr increases the prevalence of negative-stress regions.
Increasing Cr-induced negative-stress regions enhances local stabilization.
Increasing Cr-induced stabilization delays premelting relative to an equiatomic baseline.
PtPdFeCoNi nanoparticles are an example of an FCC-structured HEA suitable as the initial system.
The equiatomic initial nanoparticles exhibit a random solid solution with inherent local stress variations.
Atoms other than Cr have positive atomic stress, greater electronegativity, and greater atomic volume.
The interplay of negative-stress Cr atoms and positive-stress atoms balances the local atomic environment.
A balanced local atomic-stress environment enhances thermal stability.
Temperature-dependent chemical short-range order enhances the thermal stability of 3d HEAs.
A higher concentration or activity of Cr-induced negative-stress regions raises local energy barriers.
Raised local energy barriers delay both premelting and complete melting under thermal load.
Cr-enriched nanoparticles will have a higher premelting-onset temperature than the equiatomic baseline.
Cr-enriched nanoparticles will exhibit a delayed complete melting transition relative to the equiatomic baseline.
The proposed relationship should hold for FCC 3d-HEA nanoparticles.
The relationship may not extend to different crystal structures, intermetallic compounds, or regimes dominated by oxidation or particle-size effects.
Nanoparticle size, surface segregation, and kinetic constraints may influence premelting behavior.
Failure of increased Cr content to produce a statistically significant increase in both premelting onset and complete melting temperature would falsify the hypothesis.

contradictions.description: The exemplar initial composition PtPdFeCoNi contains no Cr, whereas the intervention, baseline, and conditions assume a system having a standard baseline Cr content that can be increased.
The initial state labels PtPdFeCoNi as a multicomponent 3d HEA, while the boundary restricts the hypothesis to 3d HEAs; Pt and Pd are not 3d transition elements.

The intervention proposes increasing the Cr fraction while keeping all other elements constant, but increasing an atomic fraction in a normalized alloy necessarily lowers at least one other fraction unless 'constant' means only that their relative ratios are fixed.
